title: Message serializer fidelity and toolcall end-to-end regression tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Build an end-to-end regression suite that validates the full round-trip fidelity of streaming message serialization, function/tool calling payloads, and structured-output schemas across runtime variants and client SDKs. Goals: 1) Detect regressions that cause dropped or reordered chunks during streaming, 2) Validate tool-call argument encoding/decoding across JSON/ndjson/stream framing, 3) Assert structured-output schema compatibility and graceful degradation when fields are missing or renamed, 4) Provide CI-level canaries that run on each runtime deploy and on PRs touching the router/streaming/serializer layers.

Background: We've had two recent incidents (incidents/2026-02-stream-split and incidents/2026-01-toolcall-truncation) where subtle changes to the framing layer and protocol normalization caused user-visible breakage in downstream callers and SDKs. This work consolidates learnings and codifies deterministic checks.

Implementation plan:
- Create a golden corpus of canonical exchanges (100+ cases) covering: short/long seqs, multi-tool chains, nested structured outputs, partial flushes, early aborts, and intentional malformed tokens for error handling. Store corpus in test-assets/golden-serializer-v1.
- Implement a harness (runtime-serializer-smoke) that can: replay golden prompts against candidate runtime (hosted/dedicated/private), capture raw wire chunks, reassemble messages, and assert chunk ordering/timings and json-schema conformance.
- Add cross-SDK playback: use python/js/go SDK test runners to exercise streaming client behavior (backpressure, chunk concat) and tool-call parsing.
- CI integration: run a fast subset (smoke 20 cases) in PRs, nightly full-suite against the latest runtime image and previous stable to catch regressions introduced by kernel/compilation changes.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype that replays ndjson-framed stream and detects out-of-order chunks (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/618). Found a non-deterministic flush ordering in the batching path.
- 2026-03-05: Decided to standardize on a canonical framing header (X-Chunk-Id + sequence) to make replay deterministic; trade-off: small protocol addition but simplifies reassembly and ops debugging. Noted backward-compat path: only enforce canonical header for CI golden runs; runtime retains legacy path for production.
- 2026-03-09: First integration test harness merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-infra/pull/223). Hooked up smoke-run to GitHub Actions; runs for linux-amd64.
- 2026-03-12: Cross-SDK runners (python/js) added; js runner surfaced an edge case in the browser chunk concat logic where Blob buffering caused message splits. Filed follow-up: ENG-77212 (browser-sdk-stream-buffer-fix).
- 2026-03-14: Nightly full-suite orchestration prototype created; needs scaling (parallelization + cost quota).

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Canonical framing vs invisible metadata: We opted for a light, opt-in canonical header in the golden corpus to minimize false positives in CI while not forcing immediate client changes. Long-term we should consider migrating SDKs to emit/validate the header.
- Depth of schema validation: Start with structural checks and known-critical fields; avoid brittle deep validation that will block minor protocol evolution. Use a layered approach: critical fields = blocking, extended fields = warnings with regression alerts.

Risk & mitigation:
- Flaky tests due to timing: mitigate by making assertions tolerant to timing variance (ordering and idempotency checks rather than strict time windows), and by recording deterministic fixtures from controlled local runs.
- Cost of nightly across all runtime variants: start with hosted + one dedicated config + previous stable; expand based on failure rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI runs smoke-suite for every PR affecting router/streaming/serializer with failure gating.
- Nightly full-suite runs and auto-opens regression issue when new failures cross a threshold.
- Cross-SDK playback validates parity for 95% of golden cases; failures triaged and assigned within 48h.

Links and artifacts:

- CI harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-infra/pull/223
- Golden corpus (internal): drive.redwood.ai/golden-serializer-v1 (internal access)
- Incident reviews: drive.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-stream-split-review.pdf

Next steps:
- Add dedicated infra tickets to parallelize nightly runs and cap cost (ENG-77205).
- Wire up regression alerting to Slack + Console dashboard with per-case failure stats (dashboard ticket ENG-77206).
- Schedule a cross-team review (runtime, SDKs, product) for 2026-03-20 to align on long-term framing migration plan.
